Plot a Scatter Chart following WJP style guidelines

Source: R/scatterChart.R
wjp_scatter.Rd

wjp_scatter() takes a data frame with one row per point and returns a ggplot object with an x-y scatter chart following WJP style guidelines, optionally split into side-by-side panels (facet). A subset of the points can be highlighted and labeled, points with small samples can be drawn hollow, and a linear trend line can be added to each panel.

Usage

wjp_scatter(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  labels = NULL,
  facet = NULL,
  highlight = NULL,
  hollow = NULL,
  colors = c("#482d8b", "#c4c4c4"),
  point_size = 7,
  trend = c("none", "lm"),
  repel = TRUE,
  seed = 1,
  repel_args = list(),
  point_stroke = 1.3,
  label_size = 9.5,
  label_fontface = "plain",
  label_colour = NULL,
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  x_breaks = NULL,
  y_breaks = NULL,
  x_labels = NULL,
  y_labels = NULL,
  x_title = NULL,
  y_title = NULL,
  facet_nrow = 1,
  strip_size = 11,
  strip_fontface = "bold.italic",
  strip_colour = NULL,
  trend_color = "#9aa0a6",
  trend_width = 0.75,
  grid_color = "#eeeeee",
  ptheme = WJP_theme()
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with one row per point.

x, y

Strings. Column names of the horizontal and vertical values.

labels

String. Column name of the point labels. Default is NULL (no labels).

facet

String. Column name of the variable that splits the chart into panels, in order of its factor levels or first appearance. Default is NULL (one panel).

highlight

Character vector of labels values to highlight. Default is NULL (all points highlighted).

hollow

String. Column name of a logical variable; TRUE draws the point as an open circle. Default is NULL.

colors

Character vector of length 2: color of the highlighted points and labels, and color of the other points. Default is the WJP violet and a light gray.

point_size

Numeric. Diameter of the points, in points. Default is 7.

trend

String. "none" (default) or "lm" (a dashed linear trend per panel).

repel

Logical. Repel labels with ggrepel when installed. Default is TRUE.

seed

Integer. Seed of the label repulsion. Default is 1.

repel_args

Named list of further arguments for ggrepel::geom_text_repel() (e.g., box.padding, force). The search runs up to max.iter iterations (max.time = 30 seconds), so the layout does not depend on the speed of the machine.

point_stroke

Numeric. Outline width of hollow points, in points. Default is 1.3.

label_size

Numeric. Size of the point labels, in points. Default is 9.5.

label_fontface

String. Font face of the point labels. Default is "plain". Weight faces such as "semibold" are accepted (see wjp_fonts()).

label_colour

String. Color of the point labels. Default is NULL (the highlight color).

xlim, ylim

Numeric vectors of length 2 with the axis limits. Default is NULL (range of the data).

x_breaks, y_breaks

Numeric vectors with the axis breaks. Default is NULL (automatic).

x_labels, y_labels

Labels of the axis breaks: a character vector or a function (e.g., function(x) paste0(x, "%")). Default is NULL (automatic).

x_title, y_title

Strings. Axis titles. Default is NULL (none).

facet_nrow

Integer. Number of rows of panels. Default is 1.

strip_size

Numeric. Size of the panel titles, in points. Default is 11.

strip_fontface

String. Font face of the panel titles. Default is "bold.italic".

strip_colour

String. Color of the panel titles. Default is NULL (the highlight color).

trend_color

String. Color of the trend line. Default is "#9aa0a6".

trend_width

Numeric. Width of the trend line, in points. Default is 0.75.

grid_color

String. Color of the grid lines. Default is "#eeeeee"; NA removes them.

ptheme

ggplot theme to apply. Default is WJP_theme().

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Points with a missing x or y are not drawn. Highlighted points (highlight) use the first color of colors and the rest use the second; when highlight is NULL every point is highlighted. Labels (labels) are drawn for the highlighted points only. With repel = TRUE and the ggrepel package installed, labels are moved away from the points and from each other with a fixed seed, so the layout is reproducible for a given figure size; otherwise they are drawn just above their points.

Points flagged by the logical column hollow (for example, estimates based on fewer than 30 observations) are drawn as open circles.

The trend (trend = "lm") is an ordinary least-squares line fitted to all the drawn points of each panel, as ggplot2::geom_smooth() with method = "lm" and no confidence band.

Sizes are given in points: point_size is the diameter of a point and point_stroke the width of the outline of hollow points.

Examples

# Always load the WJP fonts
wjp_fonts()

# Prevalence and seriousness of problems by area (fictional data)
problems <- data.frame(
  area     = rep(c("Rural", "Urban"), each = 6),
  category = rep(c("Consumer", "Housing", "Family", "Employment",
                   "Land", "Education"), 2),
  prevalence  = c(41, 9, 21, 18, 20, 9, 39, 10, 17, 19, 18, 9),
  seriousness = c(4.6, 4.3, 5.5, 6.0, 4.5, 5.6, 4.8, 4.9, 5.6, 6.4, 5.2, 5.9),
  n           = c(215, 49, 99, 96, 105, 25, 480, 126, 210, 230, 211, 104)
)
problems$small <- problems$n < 30

wjp_scatter(
  problems,
  x         = "prevalence",
  y         = "seriousness",
  labels    = "category",
  facet     = "area",
  highlight = c("Consumer", "Housing", "Family"),
  hollow    = "small",
  trend     = "lm",
  xlim      = c(0, 50),
  ylim      = c(4, 8),
  x_labels  = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
  x_title   = "Prevalence",
  y_title   = "Mean seriousness (0-10)"
)
